headline: ABITIBI METALS DRILLS 3.72% COPPER-EQ OVER 9.2M WITHIN 60.2M AT B26 — HIGH GRADES CONFIRM POLYMETALLIC THESIS IN QUÉBEC
snippet: Abitibi Metals (TSXV: AMQ) reported high-grade copper intercepts from the B26 polymetallic deposit in Québec on September 17, 2026 — hole 1274-25-366-W1 returned 3.72% CuEq (3.42% Cu, 0.26 g/t Au, 9.86 g/t Ag) over 9.2 metres within a broader 1.25% CuEq interval over 60.2 metres from 548.8 metres depth; a deep-plunge zone hole at 985 metres depth also intersected 1.45% CuEq over 14.1 metres, confirming that the B26 system remains open and continuous far below the current resource footprint with three drill rigs running through year-end.

headline: TROILUS MINES 129M AT 0.95 G/T WITHIN ITS OWN RESERVE PIT — 22M HIGH-GRADE CORE AT 3.38 G/T COULD RESHAPE QUÉBEC MINE PLAN
snippet: Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG) announced September 17, 2026 the fourth batch of results from the Z87 reserve pit optimization program at the Troilus Gold-Copper Project in north-central Québec — hole 87-26-485 returned 0.95 g/t AuEq over 129.05 metres including a high-grade core of 3.38 g/t AuEq over 22 metres within the current pit boundary, targeting inferred and historically unsampled material to improve the mine plan from the September 9 Technical Report; a second hole returned 0.99 g/t AuEq over 74.3 metres including 3.15 g/t AuEq over 3.3 metres, as the company's 40,000-metre 2026 drill campaign continues.

headline: G MINING CONFIRMS FIRST-EVER GOLD DISCOVERY AT GRODIOCAL TARGET — 23M AT 1.97 G/T AU FROM SURFACE AT BRAZIL'S GURUPI
snippet: G Mining Ventures (TSX: GMIN) confirmed a maiden gold discovery at the previously undrilled Grodiocal target within the Gurupi Project in Maranhão, Brazil on September 16, 2026 — hole GUR-26-068 intersected 23 metres at 1.97 g/t Au from 51 metres depth including 9 metres at 4.24 g/t Au; simultaneous infill at the Blanket deposit returned 79.6 metres at 1.78 g/t Au and the Mandiocal deposit returned 48.4 metres at 1.32 g/t Au including 5 metres at 3.55 g/t Au, with an updated mineral resource estimate and Preliminary Economic Assessment both targeted before year-end.

headline: ORDELL MINERALS HITS 19M AT 2.70 G/T GOLD FROM 40M DEPTH IN W.A. — 111 MORE HOLES DUE OVER 6 WEEKS, MAIDEN MRE IN Q4
snippet: Ordell Minerals (ASX: ORD) released the first 11 results from a 122-hole, 8,625-metre RC infill program at the McNabs East target of the Barimaia Gold Project in Western Australia on September 17, 2026 — standout intercepts include 32 metres at 1.65 g/t Au from 31 metres and 19 metres at 2.70 g/t Au from 40 metres, with diamond drilling confirming down-plunge continuity at 17.4 metres at 1.49 g/t Au from 220 metres; results from the remaining 111 holes are expected over the next six weeks, creating a dense pipeline of near-term news flow ahead of a maiden JORC resource estimate targeted for the December 2026 quarter.

headline: SURGE COPPER'S BERG PORPHYRY ENTERS B.C. ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT — BOTH FEDERAL AND PROVINCIAL PROCESSES FORMALLY LAUNCHED
snippet: Surge Copper (TSXV: SRGXF) announced September 16, 2026 that its Initial Project Description for the Berg Copper-Molybdenum-Silver Project in central British Columbia was accepted by both the BC Environmental Assessment Office and the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada, formally commencing provincial and federal assessment processes simultaneously; Berg is one of BC's largest undeveloped copper porphyry projects and the dual EA acceptance marks a critical de-risking milestone, with the company advancing feasibility-level engineering and environmental baseline work in parallel with the assessment.

headline: SPROTT: URANIUM MINERS UP 22% IN SEPTEMBER, SPOT HITS $82 — CAMECO FLOODING AND KAZATOMPROM CUTS DEEPEN STRUCTURAL DEFICIT
snippet: Sprott Asset Management's September uranium watch reports spot uranium rebounding to US$82/lb (up 8.05% month-to-date) with the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index up 17.01% and junior uranium miners up 21.75%, driven by simultaneous supply disruptions: Cameco cut McArthur River output guidance following northern Saskatchewan flooding and Kazatomprom reduced its 2026 production target by approximately 5%, together removing an estimated 8 million pounds from a market the World Nuclear Association projects will need to more than double its reactor capacity by 2040.

headline: COPPER RETREATS TO THREE-WEEK LOW FROM RECORD $14,533/T AS LME WAREHOUSES FILL — TARIFF UNCERTAINTY WEIGHS
snippet: Copper slipped below US$14,000 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange as fresh deliveries to exchange-tracked warehouses recorded their largest inflows in nearly four weeks, easing concern over the supply squeeze that drove the metal to an all-time record of $14,533/t on September 7; the pullback adds to uncertainty from potential U.S. tariffs on refined copper imports, though analysts note that the 17% advance over the past year — underpinned by data-centre and energy-transition demand against flat mine supply — leaves the long-term bull thesis structurally intact.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE NEARS NOVEMBER 10 EXPIRY — $6.5T IN DOWNSTREAM PRODUCTION AT RISK IF CONTROLS REINSTATED
snippet: China's suspension of its expanded October 2025 rare earth export controls expires November 10, 2026, and the global supply chain has not meaningfully diversified — China still processes approximately 99% of heavy rare earths and accounts for 69% of primary mine output, leaving an estimated $6.5 trillion of downstream manufacturing exposed to disruption; junior miners with ionic clay deposits rich in dysprosium and terbium are seeing accelerating M&A interest from Western OEMs as automotive companies invest directly in exploration to bypass China's MOFCOM licensing regime ahead of the binary November expiry date.

headline: GOLDSEEK GOLD SWOT: CHINA IMPORTING 790+ TONNES OF SILVER — SOLAR BUILD-OUT ADDS INDUSTRIAL DEMAND LAYER TO EXISTING DEFICIT
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT analysis flags China importing more than 790 tonnes of silver in the first months of 2026 as a key demand strength, driven substantially by solar photovoltaic panel production layering a structural industrial demand component onto an already six-year supply deficit; the piece identifies as a weakness the persistent speculative overhang in CFTC silver futures positioning, but notes that physical demand from the energy transition is increasingly independent of investor sentiment, making silver's current sub-$70 price a potential structural undervaluation.

headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,310, SILVER FUTURES CLIMB AFTER FED'S 12-0 VOTE FOR QUARTER-POINT HIKE — METALS SHRUG OFF FIRST RATE RISE IN THREE YEARS
snippet: Spot gold held near US$4,310 and December silver futures rose approximately 1.6% on September 17, 2026 after the Federal Reserve voted 12-0 to raise the fed funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% — its first hike since 2023 — while 16 of 18 officials pencilled in at least one additional hike before year-end; the resilience in precious metals, with silver reaching $65.52 and still up 59% over the past twelve months despite a 46% correction from its January 2026 all-time high, signals the market has fully priced the rate decision and is now focusing on fiscal fundamentals.
